an.rfft_analyzer_c_chrono.description: analyzers.lib: Standard sliding DFT of a real signal, bins 0 to N/2 (dc to Nyquist): `X(k,n) = sum(m=0..N-1) x(n-N+1+m) exp(-j*2*pi*k*m/N)`, i.e., `numpy.fft.fft(x[n-N+1:n+1])[0:N/2+1]`, recomputed every sample over the last `N` samples (rectangular window, no hop).

an.rfft_spectral_level.description: analyzers.lib: Real-signal FFT power spectrum display: passes the signal through unchanged and shows the smoothed level of each of the `N/2+1` non-negative-frequency bins in a bank of dB bargraphs.

an.spectral_centroid.description: analyzers.lib: Spectral centroid and spread of a signal, in Hz, computed from the band powers of `an.mth_octave_analyzer(O,M,ftop,N)`: the centroid is the power-weighted mean of the band center frequencies, the spread the power-weighted standard deviation around it.

an.spectral_spread.description: analyzers.lib: Spectral centroid and spread of a signal, in Hz, computed from the band powers of `an.mth_octave_analyzer(O,M,ftop,N)`: the centroid is the power-weighted mean of the band center frequencies, the spread the power-weighted standard deviation around it.

an.band_powers.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the descriptors: `band_powers(O,M,ftop,N,T)` is the bank of smoothed band powers (highest band first, like the analyzer itself), `band_center(M,ftop,N,i)` the geometric center frequency in Hz of band `i` (top and dc bands use their edges), `moment(M,ftop,N,K)` sums N band powers weighted by `center^K`, and `safe_div` divides with an epsilon-guarded denominator.

an.band_center.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the descriptors: `band_powers(O,M,ftop,N,T)` is the bank of smoothed band powers (highest band first, like the analyzer itself), `band_center(M,ftop,N,i)` the geometric center frequency in Hz of band `i` (top and dc bands use their edges), `moment(M,ftop,N,K)` sums N band powers weighted by `center^K`, and `safe_div` divides with an epsilon-guarded denominator.

an.moment.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the descriptors: `band_powers(O,M,ftop,N,T)` is the bank of smoothed band powers (highest band first, like the analyzer itself), `band_center(M,ftop,N,i)` the geometric center frequency in Hz of band `i` (top and dc bands use their edges), `moment(M,ftop,N,K)` sums N band powers weighted by `center^K`, and `safe_div` divides with an epsilon-guarded denominator.

an.safe_div.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the descriptors: `band_powers(O,M,ftop,N,T)` is the bank of smoothed band powers (highest band first, like the analyzer itself), `band_center(M,ftop,N,i)` the geometric center frequency in Hz of band `i` (top and dc bands use their edges), `moment(M,ftop,N,K)` sums N band powers weighted by `center^K`, and `safe_div` divides with an epsilon-guarded denominator.

an.spectral_flux.description: analyzers.lib: Spectral flux: the half-wave-rectified increase of each band amplitude over a `hop`-second interval, summed across the bands of `an.mth_octave_analyzer(O,M,ftop,N)`.

an.loudness_momentary.description: analyzers.lib: Momentary (400 ms window) and short-term (3 s window) loudness of an N-channel signal, in LUFS, per ITU-R BS.1770-4.

an.loudness_shortterm.description: analyzers.lib: Momentary (400 ms window) and short-term (3 s window) loudness of an N-channel signal, in LUFS, per ITU-R BS.1770-4.

an.loudness_meansquare.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the loudness meters: `loudness_meansquare(T,N)` is the channel-weighted, K-filtered mean square of an N-channel signal over a `T`-second rectangular window (the linear-domain quantity BS.1770 calls the sum of `G_i z_i`), and `meansquare2lufs` converts it to LUFS (`10*log10`, floored at -100).

an.meansquare2lufs.description: analyzers.lib: The machinery shared by the loudness meters: `loudness_meansquare(T,N)` is the channel-weighted, K-filtered mean square of an N-channel signal over a `T`-second rectangular window (the linear-domain quantity BS.1770 calls the sum of `G_i z_i`), and `meansquare2lufs` converts it to LUFS (`10*log10`, floored at -100).

an.loudness_integrated.description: analyzers.lib: Streaming approximation of the gated integrated (programme) loudness of EBU R128, in LUFS: the 400 ms mean square is accumulated under the -70 LUFS absolute gate, a relative threshold is derived 10 LU below the absolute-gated running mean, and a second accumulation under that threshold yields the integrated value.

an.true_peak.description: analyzers.lib: True-peak estimate per ITU-R BS.1770-4 Annex 2: the signal is 4x oversampled with a 48-tap polyphase windowed-sinc interpolator (12 taps per phase, Kaiser window beta = 10, each phase normalized to unity DC gain, all weights computed at compile time with `an.window_kaiser`), and the output is the largest absolute value among the four inter-sample phases.

ba.samp2sec.description: basics.lib: Converts a number of samples to a duration in seconds at the current sampling rate (see `ma.SR`).

ba.sec2samp.description: basics.lib: Converts a duration in seconds to a number of samples at the current sampling rate (see `ma.SR`).

ba.tau2pole.description: basics.lib: Returns a real pole giving exponential decay.

ba.pole2tau.description: basics.lib: Returns the time-constant, in seconds, corresponding to the given real, positive pole in (0-1).

ba.hz2midikey.description: basics.lib: Converts a frequency in Hz to a MIDI key number (MIDI key 69 = A440).

ba.hz2mel.description: basics.lib: Converts a frequency in Hz to the mel perceptual-pitch scale.

ba.mel2hz.description: basics.lib: Converts a value on the mel perceptual-pitch scale back to a frequency in Hz.

ba.semi2ratio.description: basics.lib: Converts semitones in a frequency multiplicative ratio.

ba.ratio2semi.description: basics.lib: Converts a frequency multiplicative ratio in semitones.

ba.cent2ratio.description: basics.lib: Converts cents in a frequency multiplicative ratio.

ba.ratio2cent.description: basics.lib: Converts a frequency multiplicative ratio in cents.

ba.hz2pianokey.description: basics.lib: Converts a frequency in Hz to a piano key number (piano key 49 = A440).

ba.counter.description: basics.lib: Starts counting 0, 1, 2, 3..., and raise the current integer value at each upfront of the trigger.

ba.countdown.description: basics.lib: Starts counting down from n included to 0.

ba.countup.description: basics.lib: Starts counting up from 0 to n included.

ba.sweep.description: basics.lib: Counts from 0 to `period-1` repeatedly, generating a sawtooth waveform, like `os.lf_rawsaw`, starting at 1 when `run` transitions from 0 to 1.

ba.time.description: basics.lib: A simple counter that produces the sequence of 0,1,2...N integer values.

ba.ramp.description: basics.lib: A linear ramp with a slope of '(+/-)1/n' samples to reach the next target value.

ba.line.description: basics.lib: A ramp interpolator that generates a linear transition to reach a target value:

ba.tempo.description: basics.lib: Converts a tempo in BPM into a number of samples.

ba.period.description: basics.lib: Basic sawtooth wave of period `p`.

ba.spulse.description: basics.lib: Produces a single pulse of n samples when trig goes from 0 to 1.

ba.pulsen.description: basics.lib: Pulses (like 11110000) of length `n` generated at period `p`.

ba.cycle.description: basics.lib: Split nonzero input values into `n` cycles.

ba.beat.description: basics.lib: Pulses at tempo `t` in BPM.

ba.pulse_countup_loop.description: basics.lib: Counts pulses up from 0 to n included, then starts again from 0: each pulse adds 1, the pulse after the one that reached n brings the output back to 0, and each value is held until the next pulse.

ba.pulse_countdown_loop.description: basics.lib: Counts pulses down from 0 to -n included, then starts again from 0: each pulse subtracts 1, the pulse after the one that reached -n brings the output back to 0, and each value is held until the next pulse.

ba.resetCtr.description: basics.lib: Function that lets through the mth impulse out of each consecutive group of `n` impulses.

ba.count.description: basics.lib: Count the number of elements of list l.

ba.processArray.description: basics.lib: Run `N` parallel copies of `processor`, interpolating its parameters across the copies.

ba.tabulate.description: basics.lib: Tabulate a 1D function over the range [r0, r1] for access via nearest-value, linear, cubic interpolation.

ba.tabulate_chebychev.description: basics.lib: Tabulate a 1D function over the range [r0, r1] for access via Chebyshev polynomial approximation.

ba.tabulateNd.description: basics.lib: Tabulate an nD function for access via nearest-value or linear or cubic interpolation.

ba.if.description: basics.lib: if-then-else implemented with a select2.

ba.ifNc.description: basics.lib: if-then-elseif-then-...elsif-then-else implemented on top of `ba.if`.

ba.ifNcNo.description: basics.lib: `ifNcNo(Nc,No)` is similar to `ifNc(Nc)` above but then/else branches have `No` outputs.

ba.selector.description: basics.lib: Selects the ith input among N at compile time.

ba.cselector.description: basics.lib: Selects the ith complex input among N at compile time.

ba.selectn.description: basics.lib: Selects the ith input among N at run time.

ba.selectnX.description: basics.lib: Generic form of `selectn`, with a `sel` function deciding how each pair of candidate signals is combined.

ba.selectbus.description: basics.lib: Select a bus among `NUM_BUSES` buses, where each bus has `BUS_SIZE` outputs.

ba.selectxbus.description: basics.lib: Like `ba.selectbus`, but with a cross-fade when selecting the bus using the same technique than `ba.selectmulti`.

ba.selectmulti.description: basics.lib: Selects the ith circuit among N at run time (all should have the same number of inputs and outputs) with a crossfade.

ba.selectoutn.description: basics.lib: Route input to the output among N at run time.

ba.latch.description: basics.lib: Latch input on the rising edge of trig.

ba.sAndH.description: basics.lib: Sample And Hold: "records" the input when trig is 1, outputs a frozen value when trig is 0.

ba.tAndH.description: basics.lib: Test And Hold: "records" the input when pred(input) is true, outputs a frozen value otherwise.

ba.downSample.description: basics.lib: Sample-and-hold "down sampling" effect: holds each sample for `ma.SR/freq` samples, deliberately producing aliasing ("lo-fi" decimator sound).

ba.downSampleCV.description: basics.lib: A version of `ba.downSample` where the frequency parameter has been replaced by an `amount` parameter that is in the range zero to one.

ba.peakhold.description: basics.lib: Outputs current max value above zero.

ba.peakholder.description: basics.lib: While peak-holder functions are scarcely discussed in the literature (please do send me an email if you know otherwise), common sense tells that the expected behaviour should be as follows: the absolute value of the input signal is compared with the output of the peak-holder; if the input is greater or equal to the output, a new peak is detected and sent to the output; otherwise, a timer starts and the current peak is held for N samples; once the timer is out and no new peaks have been detected, the absolute value of the current input becomes the new peak.

ba.kr2ar.description: basics.lib: Force a control rate signal to be used as an audio rate signal.

ba.impulsify.description: basics.lib: Turns each rise of a signal into a one-sample impulse as high as the rise: the output is `x - x'` when it is positive, and 0 otherwise.

ba.automat.description: basics.lib: Record and replay in a loop the successives values of the input signal.

ba.bpf.description: basics.lib: bpf is an environment (a group of related definitions) that can be used to create break-point functions.

ba.listInterp.description: basics.lib: Linearly interpolates between the elements of a list.

ba.toggle.description: basics.lib: Triggered by the change of 0 to 1, it toggles the output value between 0 and 1.

ba.on_and_off.description: basics.lib: The first channel set the output to 1, the second channel to 0.

ba.mulaw_bitcrusher.description: basics.lib: Produce distortion by reducing the signal resolution using μ-law compression.

db.DEBUG.description: debug.lib: Global switch enabling or disabling every probe in this library: 1 makes the probes active, 0 turns each of them into the identity so a fully probed patch compiles down to the unprobed one.

db.probe_slew.description: debug.lib: Slew rate probe (RMS of signal derivative).

db.probe_band_mid.description: debug.lib: Mid-band energy probe (300 Hz - 3 kHz).

db.probe_spectral_centroid.description: debug.lib: Spectral centroid estimate using multi-band analysis.

db.probe_multiband.description: debug.lib: Multi-band analyzer - outputs energy in N frequency bands.

db.probe_freq_lin.description: debug.lib: Parametric bandpass energy probe at a specific frequency.

db.probe_freq_db.description: debug.lib: Parametric bandpass energy probe in dB at a specific frequency.

db.probe_freq_ratio.description: debug.lib: Ratio between two frequency bands (useful for verifying oscillator balance).

db.probe_env_lin.description: debug.lib: Envelope state probe - outputs current envelope level for time-series capture.

db.probe_env_db.description: debug.lib: Envelope state probe in dB - for decay time analysis.

db.probe_peak_hold.description: debug.lib: Peak hold probe - captures and holds peak value until reset.

db.probe_below_threshold.description: debug.lib: Threshold crossing probe - outputs 1 when signal drops below threshold.

db.probe_attack_state.description: debug.lib: Attack phase detector - outputs 1 during attack, 0 otherwise.

db.probe_onset.description: debug.lib: Onset detector - pulses 1 at signal onset (transition from silence to sound).

db.probe_dc_precise.description: debug.lib: Precise DC offset probe with very low cutoff for accurate measurement.

db.probe_silence.description: debug.lib: Silence detector - outputs 1 when signal is effectively silent.

db.probe_sample_count.description: debug.lib: Sample counter probe - outputs current sample number (wraps at 2^24).

db.probe_time_ms.description: debug.lib: Time probe in milliseconds (wraps at ~16 seconds at 44.1kHz).

db.probe_tap.description: debug.lib: Tap a signal for side-effect analysis without changing output arity.

db.probe_tap_n.description: debug.lib: Tap an N-channel signal with a processor that takes N inputs and produces 1 output.

fi.lpt19.description: filters.lib: One-pole lowpass with a T19 time constant (approx. 19 dB attenuation after `tN` seconds).

fi.iir.description: filters.lib: Nth-order Infinite-Impulse-Response (IIR) digital filter, implemented in terms of the Transfer-Function (TF) coefficients.

fi.fir.description: filters.lib: FIR filter (convolution of FIR filter coefficients with a signal).

fi.conv.description: filters.lib: Convolution of input signal with given coefficients.

fi.convN.description: filters.lib: Convolution of input signal with given coefficients.

fi.tf1.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter.

fi.tf2.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter.

fi.tf3.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter.

fi.TF2.description: filters.lib: Tunable second-order direct-form digital filter, the "original" biquad of music.lib: y[n] = b0*x[n] + b1*x[n-1] + b2*x[n-2] - a1*y[n-1] - a2*y[n-2].

fi.tf2_tpt.description: filters.lib: Second-order digital filter `N(z)/A(z)`, with `A(z) = 1 + a1 z^-1 + a2 z^-2` and `N(z) = n0 + n1 z^-1 + n2 z^-2`, realized as a trapezoidal (topology-preserving) state-variable filter with exactly the same poles and zeros.

fi.notchw.description: filters.lib: Simple notch filter based on a biquad, realized with `tf2_tpt`.

fi.tf21.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter where:

fi.tf22.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter where:

fi.tf22t.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter where:

fi.tf21t.description: filters.lib: tfN = N'th-order direct-form digital filter where:

fi.av2sv.description: filters.lib: Compute reflection coefficients sv from transfer-function denominator av.

fi.bvav2nuv.description: filters.lib: Compute lattice tap coefficients from transfer-function coefficients.

fi.iir_lat2.description: filters.lib: Two-multiply lattice IIR filter of arbitrary order.

fi.allpassnt.description: filters.lib: Two-multiply lattice allpass (nested order-1 direct-form-ii allpasses), with taps.

fi.iir_kl.description: filters.lib: Kelly-Lochbaum ladder IIR filter of arbitrary order.

fi.iir_lat1.description: filters.lib: One-multiply lattice IIR filter of arbitrary order.

fi.allpassn1mt.description: filters.lib: One-multiply lattice allpass with tap lines.

fi.iir_nl.description: filters.lib: Normalized ladder filter of arbitrary order.

fi.allpassnnlt.description: filters.lib: Normalized ladder allpass filter of arbitrary order.

fi.tf2np.description: filters.lib: Biquad based on a stable second-order Normalized Ladder Filter (more robust to modulation than `tf2` and protected against instability).

fi.wgr.description: filters.lib: Second-order transformer-normalized digital waveguide resonator.

fi.nlf2.description: filters.lib: Second order normalized digital waveguide resonator.

fi.apnl.description: filters.lib: Passive Nonlinear Allpass based on Pierce switching springs idea.

fi.scat.description: filters.lib: Scatter off of reflectance r with reflection coefficient s.

fi.allpassnn.description: filters.lib: Normalized form - four multiplies and two adds per section, but coefficients can be time varying and nonlinear without "parametric amplification" (modulation of signal energy).

fi.allpassnkl.description: filters.lib: Kelly-Lochbaum form - four multiplies and two adds per section, but all signals have an immediate physical interpretation as traveling pressure waves, etc.

fi.allpassn1m.description: filters.lib: One-multiply form - one multiply and three adds per section.

fi.allpass1_noclip.description: filters.lib: First- and second-order direct-form allpass filters with clipping prevention (Fontana et al., DAFx26, Algorithms 1 and 2).

fi.allpass2_noclip.description: filters.lib: First- and second-order direct-form allpass filters with clipping prevention (Fontana et al., DAFx26, Algorithms 1 and 2).

fi.tf2s.description: filters.lib: Second-order digital filter, specified by ANALOG transfer-function polynomials B(s)/A(s), and a frequency-scaling parameter.

fi.tf2snp.description: filters.lib: Second-order digital filter, specified by ANALOG transfer-function polynomials B(s)/A(s), and a frequency-scaling parameter.

fi.tf1snp.description: filters.lib: First-order special case of tf2snp above: a first-order normalized ladder, with its reflection coefficient, complement and tap gains computed from the analog coefficients without cancellation, like tf2snp.

fi.tf3slf.description: filters.lib: Analogous to `tf2s` above, but third order, and using the typical low-frequency-matching bilinear-transform constant 2/T ("lf" series) instead of the specific-frequency-matching value used in `tf2s` and `tf1s`.

fi.tf1s.description: filters.lib: First-order direct-form digital filter, specified by ANALOG transfer-function polynomials B(s)/A(s), and a frequency-scaling parameter.

fi.tf2s_df.description: filters.lib: Direct-form versions of `tf2s` and `tf1s`: the same bilinear transform of B(s)/A(s), prewarped at `w1`, realized as the direct-form biquad `tf2` and first-order section `tf1`.

fi.tf1s_df.description: filters.lib: Direct-form versions of `tf2s` and `tf1s`: the same bilinear transform of B(s)/A(s), prewarped at `w1`, realized as the direct-form biquad `tf2` and first-order section `tf1`.

fi.tpt_df_fmin.description: filters.lib: The lowest cutoff, in Hz, at which the `*_tpt_df` functions below switch from trapezoidal (TPT) sections to the cheaper direct-form ones (`tf2s_df`, `tf1s_df`) in the precision being compiled: 2304 Hz in single precision, 0 (direct form everywhere) in double, quad and fixed-point precision.

fi.tf2sb.description: filters.lib: Bandpass mapping of `tf2s`: In addition to a frequency-scaling parameter `w1` (set to the desired passband width in rad/sec: the prototype's cutoff at 1 rad/sec maps to two band edges `w1` apart), there is a desired center-frequency parameter wc (also in rad/s).

fi.tf1sb.description: filters.lib: First-to-second-order lowpass-to-bandpass section mapping, analogous to tf2sb above.

fi.resonlp.description: filters.lib: Simple resonant lowpass filter based on `tf2s` (virtual analog).

fi.resonhp.description: filters.lib: Simple resonant highpass filters based on `tf2s` (virtual analog).

fi.resonbp.description: filters.lib: Simple resonant bandpass filters based on `tf2s` (virtual analog).

fi.lowpass0_highpass1.description: filters.lib: Generic Butterworth lowpass/highpass filter: the shared implementation behind `fi.lowpass` and `fi.highpass`, with a selector choosing between the two responses.

fi.lowpass_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `lowpass` and `highpass` (order-`N` Butterworth) in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`, `tf1s_df`) at and above it.

fi.highpass_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `lowpass` and `highpass` (order-`N` Butterworth) in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`, `tf1s_df`) at and above it.

fi.highpass_plus_lowpass.description: filters.lib: Sum of the order-`N` Butterworth highpass and lowpass responses at the same cutoff: for odd `N`, an allpass used as delay equalizer by `fi.filterbank` and the filter banks below.

fi.highpass_minus_lowpass.description: filters.lib: Difference between the order-`N` Butterworth highpass and lowpass responses at the same cutoff: an allpass used as delay equalizer by the dc-inverted filter banks (`fi.mth_octave_filterbank_alt`).

fi.highpass_plus_lowpass_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `highpass_plus_lowpass` and `highpass_minus_lowpass` in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`, `tf1s_df`) at and above it, as in `lowpass_tpt_df`: the delay equalizers of the `*_tpt_df` filter banks.

fi.highpass_minus_lowpass_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `highpass_plus_lowpass` and `highpass_minus_lowpass` in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`, `tf1s_df`) at and above it, as in `lowpass_tpt_df`: the delay equalizers of the `*_tpt_df` filter banks.

fi.highpass_plus_lowpass_even.description: filters.lib: Sum of the even-order Butterworth highpass and lowpass responses, `highpass(N,fc) + lowpass(N,fc)`.

fi.highpass_minus_lowpass_even.description: filters.lib: Difference between the even-order Butterworth highpass and lowpass responses, `highpass(N,fc) - lowpass(N,fc)`.

fi.highpass_plus_lowpass_odd.description: filters.lib: Sum of the odd-order highpass and lowpass responses.

fi.highpass_minus_lowpass_odd.description: filters.lib: Difference between the odd-order highpass and lowpass responses.

fi.lowpass6e_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `lowpass6e` and `highpass6e` in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`) at and above it, as in `lowpass_tpt_df`: the band splits of `an.mth_octave_analyzer6e_tpt_df`.

fi.highpass6e_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `lowpass6e` and `highpass6e` in trapezoidal sections below the cutoff limit `L` and in direct-form sections (`tf2s_df`) at and above it, as in `lowpass_tpt_df`: the band splits of `an.mth_octave_analyzer6e_tpt_df`.

fi.bandpass.description: filters.lib: Order 2*Nh Butterworth bandpass filter made using the transformation `s <- s + wc^2/s` on `lowpass(Nh)`, where `wc` is the desired bandpass center frequency.

fi.bandstop.description: filters.lib: Order 2*Nh Butterworth bandstop filter made using the transformation `s <- s + wc^2/s` on `highpass(Nh)`, where `wc` is the desired bandpass center frequency.

fi.bandpass0_bandstop1.description: filters.lib: Generic Butterworth bandpass/bandstop filter: the shared implementation behind `fi.bandpass` and `fi.bandstop`, with a selector choosing between the two responses.

fi.bandpass6e.description: filters.lib: Order 6 elliptic bandpass filter analogous to `bandpass(3)`: a third-order elliptic lowpass prototype mapped to a bandpass, with a 0.2 dB equiripple passband between `fl` and `fu`.

fi.bandpass12e.description: filters.lib: Order 12 elliptic bandpass filter analogous to `bandpass(6)`: a sixth-order elliptic lowpass prototype mapped to a bandpass, with a 0.2 dB equiripple passband between `fl` and `fu`.

fi.pospass6e.description: filters.lib: Positive-pass filter like `pospass`, but built on the order-6 elliptic lowpass `lowpass6e` instead of a Butterworth lowpass: a steeper transition band for the same order.

fi.hilbert.description: filters.lib: Approximate Hilbert transform: twice the imaginary part of the analytic signal computed by `fi.pospass`, i.e. a signal in quadrature (-90 degrees) with the in-phase (real) output of the same filter.

fi.lowshelf.description: filters.lib: Order-`N` "low shelf" filter (gain boost|cut between dc and some frequency) `low_shelf` is a standard Faust function.

fi.low_shelf.description: filters.lib: Default low shelf filter: 3rd-order Butterworth case of `fi.lowshelf` (`low_shelf = lowshelf(3)`), boosting or cutting by `L0` dB between dc and `fx`.

fi.low_shelf1.description: filters.lib: First-order low shelf filter, an optimized special case of `fi.lowshelf(1)`: boosts or cuts by `L0` dB between dc and `fx`.

fi.low_shelf1_l.description: filters.lib: First-order low shelf filter like `fi.low_shelf1`, but taking a LINEAR gain `G0` instead of a level in dB (avoids computing `ba.db2linear` at run time when the gain is already linear).

fi.lowshelf_other_freq.description: filters.lib: Second corner frequency of a low shelf: given the shelf order `N`, level `L0` and transition frequency `fx` of `fi.lowshelf(N,L0,fx)`, returns the frequency at which the response returns to 0 dB (see the "Shelf Shape" section of `fi.lowshelf`).

fi.highshelf.description: filters.lib: Order-`N` "high shelf" filter (gain boost|cut above some frequency).

fi.high_shelf.description: filters.lib: Default high shelf filter: 3rd-order Butterworth case of `fi.highshelf` (`high_shelf = highshelf(3)`), boosting or cutting by `Lpi` dB between `fx` and SR/2.

fi.high_shelf1.description: filters.lib: First-order high shelf filter, an optimized special case of `fi.highshelf(1)`: boosts or cuts by `Lpi` dB between `fx` and SR/2.

fi.high_shelf1_l.description: filters.lib: First-order high shelf filter like `fi.high_shelf1`, but taking a LINEAR gain `Gpi` instead of a level in dB.

fi.highshelf_other_freq.description: filters.lib: Second corner frequency of a high shelf: given the shelf order `N`, level `Lpi` and transition frequency `fx` of `fi.highshelf(N,Lpi,fx)`, returns the frequency at which the response leaves 0 dB.

fi.peak_eq.description: filters.lib: Second order "peaking equalizer" section (gain boost or cut near some frequency) Also called a "parametric equalizer" section.

fi.peak_eq_cq.description: filters.lib: Constant-Q second order peaking equalizer section.

fi.peak_eq_rm.description: filters.lib: Regalia-Mitra second order peaking equalizer section: `H(z) = (1 + A(z))/2 + K (1 - A(z))/2`, with `A(z)` the second order allpass centered at `fx` and `K = 10^(Lfx/20)`.

fi.spectral_tilt.description: filters.lib: Spectral tilt filter, providing an arbitrary spectral rolloff factor alpha in (-1,1), where -1 corresponds to one pole (-6 dB per octave), and +1 corresponds to one zero (+6 dB per octave).

fi.mth_octave_filterbank[n].description: filters.lib: Allpass-complementary filter banks based on Butterworth band-splitting.

fi.mth_octave_filterbank.description: filters.lib: Allpass-complementary filter banks based on Butterworth band-splitting.

fi.mth_octave_filterbank_tpt_df.description: filters.lib: `mth_octave_filterbank` and `mth_octave_filterbank_alt` with an explicit cutoff limit `L`, as `filterbank_tpt_df` is to `filterbank`: `mth_octave_filterbank(O,M,ftop,N)` is `mth_octave_filterbank_tpt_df(tpt_df_fmin,O,M,ftop,N)`, and likewise for the `_alt` version (and so for `mth_octave_filterbank3`, `5` and `_default`).

ma.SR.description: maths.lib: Current sampling rate given at init time, between 50 and 192000 Hz (see `pl.SR`).

ma.PI.description: maths.lib: Constant PI in double precision.

ma.E.description: maths.lib: Constant e in double precision.

ma.EPSILON.description: maths.lib: Constant EPSILON available in simple/double/quad precision, as defined in the [floating-point standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_754) and [machine epsilon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_epsilon), that is smallest positive number such that `1.0 + EPSILON != 1.0`.

ma.MIN.description: maths.lib: Constant MIN available in simple/double/quad precision (minimal positive value).

ma.MAX.description: maths.lib: Constant MAX available in simple/double/quad precision (maximal positive value).

ma.INFINITY.description: maths.lib: Obsolete alias of `MAX`, kept for compatibility reasons.

ma.FTZ.description: maths.lib: Flush to zero: force samples under the "maximum subnormal number" to be zero.

ma.copysign.description: maths.lib: Changes the sign of x (first input) to that of y (second input).

ma.neg.description: maths.lib: Invert the sign (-x) of a signal.

ma.not.description: maths.lib: Bitwise `not` of an integer input signal, implemented with [xor](https://faustdoc.grame.fr/manual/syntax/#xor-primitive) as `not(x) = x xor -1;`.

ma.sub.description: maths.lib: Subtracts the first input `x` from the second input `y`: the output is `y - x`.

ma.inv.description: maths.lib: Compute the inverse (1/x) of the input signal x (non-zero).

ma.cbrt.description: maths.lib: Computes the cube root of of the input signal.

ma.hypot.description: maths.lib: Computes the euclidian distance of the two input signals x and y, sqrt(x*x+y*y), without undue overflow or underflow.

ma.ldexp.description: maths.lib: Takes two input signals: x and n (an integer), and multiplies x by 2 to the power n.

ma.scalb.description: maths.lib: Takes two input signals: x and n (an integer), and multiplies x by 2 to the power n.

ma.log1p.description: maths.lib: Computes log(1 + x) of the input signal x (greater than -1) without undue loss of accuracy when x is nearly zero, where `log(1 + x)` loses all its digits in single precision.

ma.logb.description: maths.lib: Return exponent of the (positive) input signal as a floating-point number.

ma.ilogb.description: maths.lib: Return exponent of the (positive) input signal as an integer number.

ma.log2.description: maths.lib: Returns the base 2 logarithm of the positive input signal x.

ma.expm1.description: maths.lib: Return exponent of the input signal x minus 1, `exp(x) - 1`, with better precision near 0, where `exp(x) - 1` loses all its digits in single precision.

ma.acosh.description: maths.lib: Computes the principle value of the inverse hyperbolic cosine of the input signal (greater than or equal to 1).

ma.asinh.description: maths.lib: Computes the inverse hyperbolic sine of the input signal.

ma.atanh.description: maths.lib: Computes the inverse hyperbolic tangent of the input signal, in (-1, 1).

ma.sinh.description: maths.lib: Computes the hyperbolic sine of the input signal.

ma.cosh.description: maths.lib: Computes the hyperbolic cosine of the input signal.

ma.tanh.description: maths.lib: Computes the hyperbolic tangent of the input signal.

ma.erf.description: maths.lib: Computes the error function of the input signal.

ma.erfc.description: maths.lib: Computes the complementary error function of the input signal.

ma.gamma.description: maths.lib: Computes the gamma function of the positive input signal.

ma.lgamma.description: maths.lib: Calculates the natural logorithm of the absolute value of the gamma function of the positive input signal.

ma.J0.description: maths.lib: Computes the Bessel function of the first kind of order 0 of the input signal.

ma.J1.description: maths.lib: Computes the Bessel function of the first kind of order 1 of the input signal.

ma.Jn.description: maths.lib: Computes the Bessel function of the first kind of order n (first input signal, an integer) of the second input signal x.

ma.Y0.description: maths.lib: Computes the linearly independent Bessel function of the second kind of order 0 of the positive input signal.

ma.Y1.description: maths.lib: Computes the linearly independent Bessel function of the second kind of order 1 of the positive input signal.

ma.Yn.description: maths.lib: Computes the linearly independent Bessel function of the second kind of order n (first input signal, an integer) of the second input signal x (positive).

ma.fabs.description: maths.lib: Aliases of the `abs`, `max` and `min` primitives, for compatibility with the C math library naming: `fabs = abs`, `fmax = max`, `fmin = min`.

ma.fmax.description: maths.lib: Aliases of the `abs`, `max` and `min` primitives, for compatibility with the C math library naming: `fabs = abs`, `fmax = max`, `fmin = min`.

ma.fmin.description: maths.lib: Aliases of the `abs`, `max` and `min` primitives, for compatibility with the C math library naming: `fabs = abs`, `fmax = max`, `fmin = min`.

ma.np2.description: maths.lib: Gives the next power of 2 of x.

ma.frac.description: maths.lib: Gives the fractional part of n.

ma.decimal.description: maths.lib: Gives the fractional part of n.

ma.modulo.description: maths.lib: Modulus operation using the `(x%y+y)%y` formula to ensures the result is always non-negative, even if `x` is negative.

ma.isnan.description: maths.lib: Return non-zero if x is a NaN.

ma.isinf.description: maths.lib: Return non-zero if x is a positive or negative infinity.

ma.chebychev.description: maths.lib: Chebychev transformation of order N.

ma.chebychevpoly.description: maths.lib: Linear combination of the first Chebyshev polynomials.

ma.diffn.description: maths.lib: Negated first-order difference of the input signal x: `x' - x`.

ma.signum.description: maths.lib: The signum function signum(x) is defined as -1 for x<0, 0 for x==0, and 1 for x>0.

ma.nextpow2.description: maths.lib: The nextpow2(x) returns the lowest integer m such that 2^m >= x.

ma.zc.description: maths.lib: Indicator function for zero-crossing of the input signal: it returns 1 if a zero-crossing occurs, 0 otherwise.

ma.primes.description: maths.lib: Return the n-th prime using a waveform primitive, n being the (0-based) input signal.
